verdict.rationale: Docs show strong typed-agent design (Agent[DepsType, OutputType] generics, IDE-checked types, Pydantic output_type that 'forces' model responses to match schema), which is exactly the kind of build-time/schema safety the story asks for. But hands-on reports contradict reliability: users report structured output frequently fails to validate even with retries, and one engineer says vanilla pydantic-ai 'rarely creates objects successfully regardless of retries,' while another found structured output broken for certain providers. missing for 10: independent verification that schema validation reliably prevents agent errors, and resolution of the reported structured-output failure cases.
